description: Add a size-specialized n=1024 path for the batch-60 benchmark terms on the robust four-size solver: use a B200 multi-CTA two-stage dense-to-band Householder reduction, tensor-core compact-WY updates, parallel tridiagonal solve and reflector backtransform, plus a cheap structure gate, exact certificate, and selective Xsyev repair while preserving existing custom sizes.

Generalized the packed lower-triangle Householder reducer and 16-eigenpair parallel tridiagonal solve to n=1024, then applied the existing FP32 blocked compact-WY backtransform, exact certificate, two Newton-Schulz/Rayleigh refinements, and selective Xsyev repair. All 39 tests pass, but full geomean regresses from 39012.589 to 48881.484 us: n1024 terms are 153833/221809/261098/258533 us. Standard n1024 profile is 112.856 ms reducer, 17.356 ms solve, roughly 14 ms backtransform/certificate, with no library repair visible.

Replaced the first 512 n1024 Householder columns with a four-CTA x 768-thread SM100 cluster that cooperatively packs lower storage, shares v/y through DSM, and distributes symmetric matvec and rank-2 updates before the proven one-CTA tail. All 39 tests pass. Full metric improves from 48881.484 to 46512.675 us; mixed/nearrank/geometric n1024 improve from 221809/261098/258533 to 171862/210372/207140 us, while standard rises from 153833 to 159239 us.

Forced up to four FP32 Newton-Schulz/Rayleigh cleanup passes for unsafe n1024 matrices instead of applying the early repair heuristic. All tests pass. This removes standard-case Xsyev repair and cuts it from 159239 to 105410 us, but mixed/nearrank/geometric rise from 171862/210372/207140 to 185854/242926/239716 us as harder spectra pay added refinement before repair; aggregate improves slightly to 46358.302 us.

Expanded the n1024 clustered prefix from 512 to 768 columns and raised its four CTAs from 768 to 1024 threads, leaving only a quarter-size one-CTA tail. All tests pass, but aggregate regresses from 46358.302 to 47659.015 us; standard/mixed/nearrank/geometric n1024 become 121075/203571/260936/258120 us. The wider clustered interval and 128-warp geometry cost more synchronization and cleanup than they save.

Restored the faster four-CTA x 768-thread, 512-column cluster and routed only n1024 blocked compact-WY reflector backtransforms through PyTorch high-precision tensor-core GEMMs; n512 remains strict FP32. Exact certificate plus forced FP32 cleanup passes all 39 tests. Aggregate improves slightly from 46358.302 to 46324.236 us; standard is unchanged at 105491 us and mixed/nearrank/geometric are 186301/240392/237172 us.

Changed the 512-column n1024 prefix from four 768-thread CTAs to two 1024-thread CTAs so all 60 matrices fit in one SM cluster wave. All tests pass, but reduced per-matrix parallelism dominates: standard/mixed/nearrank/geometric rise to 118321/200060/255025/251705 us and aggregate regresses to 47368.419 us versus 46324.236 for four CTAs.

Restored the four-CTA reducer and specialized n1024 tridiagonal solve to 25 eigenpairs per 128-thread block with four-lane groups and a 26-float shared pitch, versus 16 eigenpairs/eight lanes previously. Inactive tail groups are guarded; existing size templates remain unchanged. All tests pass and every n1024 term improves to 99920/180271/234267/231650 us; aggregate drops from 46324.236 to 45779.798 us.

Added an n1024 diagonal-structure gate: low peakiness or strongly positive trace identifies planted-spectrum/PSD batches, and any flagged matrix routes the whole batch to BF16x9 Xsyev to avoid serial underfilled custom-plus-library work. Dense row-scaled batches retain the clustered solver and exact certificate. All tests pass. Mixed falls from 223397 to 106335 us, near-rank/geometric remain 105764/102678 us, standard custom is 99792 us, and aggregate improves from parent 39012.589 to 38841.882 us.

Extended the four-CTA x 768-thread n1024 clustered reducer prefix from 512 to 640 columns while keeping the 25-eigenpair solve, tensor-core WY backtransform, structure gate, and exact cleanup fixed. All tests pass. Standard n1024 drops from 99792 to 95638 us; the three gated terms remain about 102.7-106.3 ms, and aggregate improves from 38841.882 to 38705.740 us.

Extended the four-CTA x 768-thread n1024 cluster prefix from 640 to 768 columns. All 39 tests pass. Standard n1024 improves from 95638 to 94545 us while gated terms stay 102.7-106.3 ms; full geomean improves from 38705.740 to 38653.791 us, with some favorable unrelated n2048/n352 variance in this sample.

Extended the four-CTA n1024 cluster prefix from 768 to 896 columns to bracket the shrinking-tail crossover. All tests pass, but standard regresses from 94545 to 94821 us; aggregate 38661.711 us is statistically tied only because unrelated n2048/n512 terms ran faster. The measured cutoff minimum is at or below 768 columns.

Restored the selected 768-column cluster and ran the first two n1024 Newton-Schulz/Rayleigh cleanup passes with tensor-core high matmul precision, restoring strict FP32 before each exact certificate and for later cleanup. All tests pass. Standard n1024 drops from 94545 to 88739 us; gated terms remain 102.6-106.6 ms, and aggregate improves from 38653.791 to 38516.956 us (1.27% below parent 39012.589).

Moved the third n1024 cleanup iteration from strict FP32 to tensor-core high precision while leaving a fourth strict pass available. All tests pass, but the tensor pass does not clear the exact certificate and standard rises from 88739 to 89950 us; aggregate is 38536.981 us versus 38516.956 for two tensor plus one strict pass.

Raised each of the four n1024 cluster CTAs from 768 to 896 threads at the selected 768-column cutoff while restoring the selected two-tensor/one-FP32 cleanup schedule. All tests pass, but standard regresses sharply from 88739 to 114406 us and aggregate to 39226.555 us; 768-thread blocks retain the better cluster residency balance.

Used the B200's 232448-byte opt-in shared-memory limit to raise the n1024 tridiagonal solve from 25 eigenpairs/pitch26/41 tiles to 26 eigenpairs/pitch27/40 tiles at 229376 bytes. Restored selected 4x768 reduction and two tensor cleanup passes. All tests pass; standard improves marginally from 88739 to 88641 us and aggregate sample improves to 38458.038 us, with most additional movement from unrelated size variance.

Replaced n1024 certify-after-each-refinement compaction with a fixed two-tensor plus one-strict all-batch Newton-Schulz/Rayleigh pipeline, followed by one exact certificate and at most one selective strict refinement before Xsyev. All tests pass. Standard improves from 88641 to 88270 us; aggregate is 38485.488 us, statistically tied with 38458.038 because unrelated terms moved.

Reduced n1024 tridiagonal bisection from 25 to 24 iterations. All 39 tests pass, but the standard batch-60 n1024 term rises from about 88270 to 145630 us, indicating the looser eigenvalue estimates trigger the selective repair/Xsyev path; aggregate regresses to 39971.758 us. Retain 25 iterations.

Restored the required 25 n1024 bisection iterations and removed the unused post-certificate selective refinement from the fixed two-tensor/one-strict pipeline, falling directly back to Xsyev only if the exact certificate fails. All 39 tests pass; standard is 88123.624 us and aggregate is a new sample best of 38423.601 us.

Replaced clustered n1024 flat packed-index copying and per-element sqrtf row inversion with a coalesced warp-per-row traversal. All 39 tests pass, but row-length imbalance raises standard from 88124 to 90782 us and aggregate to 38557.861 us; retain the flat packed traversal.

Kept flat balanced clustered packing but computed one packed-row sqrt per warp chunk and adjusted lanes at row boundaries. All 39 tests pass, yet the longer-lived mapping state likely increases reducer register pressure: standard rises to 108312 us and aggregate to 39059.351 us. Retain the minimal per-index mapping.

Restored minimal flat packing and doubled clustered Householder dot groups from 8 to 16 lanes. All 39 tests pass, but lower row concurrency raises standard n1024 from 88124 to 98338 us and aggregate to 38767.404 us; 8 lanes is superior.

Narrowed clustered Householder dot groups from 16 to 4 lanes to maximize row concurrency. All 39 tests pass, but changed accumulation error triggers certificate repair on standard n1024, which rises to 150789 us; aggregate regresses to 40095.477 us. Eight lanes is the stable optimum among 4/8/16.

Restored the stable 8-lane clustered dots and replaced standalone reflector unpack's per-element sqrtf packed-row inversion with a cyclic warp-per-row traversal. All 39 tests pass; standard n1024 improves marginally from 88124 to 88076 us while aggregate 38445.588 remains noise-tied because unrelated terms moved. Profile the 0.912 ms unpack component directly.

Restored balanced flat reflector unpack and raised its launch from 256 to 1024 threads so each of the 60 matrix CTAs occupies its SM. All 39 tests pass; standard n1024 improves materially from 88124 to 87351 us. Aggregate 38427.445 is tied with 38423.601 because the unchanged n2048 term moved upward.

Final commit 81aa5a46ee3bc94989b81d54eb313bf7fa1dba4a validates all 39 tests and measures 38427.445 us overall versus parent 39012.589 us. Best aggregate sample was 38423.601 at b1c6563b4; final source is retained because its n1024 standard term is stronger at 87350.677 us versus 88123.624 us, with unrelated n2048 noise explaining the aggregate tie. Implemented a B200 4-CTA x768-thread clustered packed Householder prefix through column 768, one-CTA tail, 40-way parallel 26-eigenpair tridiagonal tiles using 229376 B shared memory, tensor-core compact-WY backtransform and two high-precision cleanup passes, one strict cleanup, structure gate, exact certificate, and Xsyev fallback; existing sizes still pass. Final nsys: clustered reducer 56.979 ms, tridiagonal solve 11.303 ms, tail 1.864 ms, unpack 0.247 ms after raising it to 1024 threads (down from 0.912 ms), certificate 0.277 ms. Tested and rejected 2-CTA/4-CTA block geometries, prefix cutoffs 512/640/768/896, 4/8/16-lane dot groups, 24 bisection steps, extra cleanup schedules, and alternate packed-copy traversals. Keep pushing: the concrete openings are a genuinely blocked tensor-core dense-to-band reducer to replace the serial column dependency, fewer cluster barriers/DSM copies through panelized Householders, fused strict cleanup plus exact certificate, a faster robust 25-step tridiagonal solver, calibrated per-matrix structure routing, and fusion of tail/unpack/backtransform. This branch should also be combined with the fleet's strongest n352/n512 work.
